Relevance to the AI supply chain: High-value chips, components and time-sensitive shipments
Disruption mechanism: Airspace restrictions, airport outages and cargo-capacity constraints
Alternatives and limitations: Alternative airports or flight paths; sea freight where timing and handling permit
Notes: Transport-mode overview, not an estimate of the share of AI chips shipped by air.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Regional shipping and access to Taiwan's ports and industrial inputs
Disruption mechanism: Conflict, blockade, port disruption and higher insurance costs
Alternatives and limitations: Some through-traffic can reroute; a blockade or interrupted fabrication cannot be solved by rerouting alone
Notes: Through-traffic and deliveries to Taiwan face different risks. No current route-availability assessment is implied.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Shipping and energy flows between the Indian and Pacific Oceans
Disruption mechanism: Congestion, accidents, security incidents or conflict
Alternatives and limitations: Sunda or Lombok routes where vessel dimensions and navigation conditions permit, with longer journeys
Notes: A broad trade and energy corridor; this is not an AI-specific shipment map.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Asia-Europe container traffic, machinery and industrial inputs
Disruption mechanism: Canal blockage, attacks, conflict or carrier avoidance
Alternatives and limitations: Cape of Good Hope routing; air freight for suitable high-value cargo
Notes: Alternative routes increase distance and cost. Availability changes with security conditions.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) flows affecting energy markets
Disruption mechanism: Conflict, shipping interruption and higher freight or insurance costs
Alternatives and limitations: Some oil can use bypass pipelines; other suppliers and reserves offer limited short-term relief
Notes: Primarily an indirect energy exposure. Oil pipelines do not replace LNG shipping capacity.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Electronics, servers and industrial goods moving between Asia and North America
Disruption mechanism: Port disruption, trade restrictions, congestion and capacity shortages
Alternatives and limitations: Alternative ports and inland connections; limited air freight for suitable cargo
Notes: A network of routes, not a single chokepoint. Rerouting does not remove trade restrictions.

Relevance to the AI supply chain: Some Asia-North America East Coast routes and other interoceanic trade
Disruption mechanism: Water shortages, draft restrictions and reduced transit capacity
Alternatives and limitations: West Coast ports with inland transport, or longer ocean routes where commercially and operationally viable
Notes: Not all Asia-Americas shipments use Panama. Suez is an option only when route conditions permit.
